bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains an IPv4 header from libpcap's caplen-bounded packet buffer, and rewrites the packet before replay. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the packet-controlled IPv4 total-length field (ntohs(ip_len) minus ip_hl) without proving that the claimed length fits the captured buffer. do_checksum_liveplay forwards that length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose loop reads successive 16-bit words until the claimed length is exhausted. A crafted pcap can therefore claim an IP length larger than caplen and make the checksum loop read past libpcap's heap buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 imported tcpliveplay.c as a new 1,303-line file and, in the same commit, added the complete vulnerable path: main calls rewrite on argv[2], rewrite consumes pcap_next_ex packet buffers and calls fix_all_checksum_newconn, fix_all_checksum_newconn trusts ip_len for the checksum length, and do_checksum_math_newconn walks that length without a caplen bound. Later commits only renamed the *_newconn helpers to *_liveplay or reformatted the same calculation, so the import commit is the smallest repository commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism.

evidence: Advisory lifecycle: GHSA-6cvx-mw62-87pq/CVE-2025-51005 and NVD identify tcpreplay 4.5.1, src/tcpliveplay.c do_checksum_math_liveplay, and a crafted-pcap heap-buffer-overflow; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/925 includes the ASan read at line 1175 and explains that ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) minus the IP-header length can be large. Attack path and BIC: `git grep -n` at 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 finds main's rewrite call at src/tcpliveplay.c:229, pcap_next_ex at :1013, the checksum call at :1097, the unbounded ip_len-derived length at :1193, forwarding to checksum math at :1258, and its 16-bit read loop at :1289. `git log master -L 1123,1139:src/tcpliveplay.c` traces the present calculation through formatting commit 8f3761d212d39d82a3f2cad39f9f92c1ebc3ca5c, spelling/whitespace changes, and rename commit e5039a91fbf018b5c7d084224c884e2275529724 to the new-file addition in 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01; none of the later commits first creates the mechanism. Parent absence: the BIC commit object names the sole parent e7f6ea96f6531bb71b68b206140ef033ff16f5fa, and `git cat-file -e e7f6ea96f6531bb71b68b206140ef033ff16f5fa:src/tcpliveplay.c` fails because the path is absent, directly proving the vulnerable source and lines are absent from the immediate parent tree. Decomposition: the BIC is a one-parent ordinary commit with no squash/member trailers; it imports an independently developed file (the file header credits Yazan H. Siam and dates it September 5, 2012), but the validated repository contains no smaller member SHA to decompose, so squash_decomposed is false and decomposed_shas is empty. Version boundary: v4.5.1 resolves to 0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e, `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e` exits 0, and `git grep` at v4.5.1 shows the vulnerable ip_len calculation at src/tcpliveplay.c:1085 and :1092. There is no patched boundary: vendor comments on issue #925 say updates were shelved rather than fixed; v4.6.1 still has the vulnerable calculation at :1129; current validated HEAD c3f6049a1de91e7d3b81543d0ecb01e465b05214 still has it at :1129 and passes it to checksum math at :1188; configure.ac still enables tcpliveplay on Linux. Commit e516e93a176d9b9e170e19c96b01be4e5b29e9fe fixes different tcpliveplay OOB mechanisms for GHSA-4hqm-8v2c-9pwj and adds only a minimum-header caplen check, not the required ip_len-versus-caplen bound, so it is not a fix for this CVE. The case is therefore unpatched in the available full history and both fix fields are null.
reasoning: The vulnerability is reached before replay scheduling while rewrite processes the attacker's pcap: libpcap provides a finite captured buffer, but the imported checksum caller substitutes the IPv4 header's untrusted total length for the actual captured extent, and the checksum loop dereferences according to that larger value. Line history makes 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 the causal BIC rather than the 2012 helper rename, later refactors, releases, or the unrelated 2026 hardening commit: it adds the packet-reader call path, unchecked length derivation, and over-reading loop together, while its immediate parent has no tcpliveplay.c at all. The BIC is already an ancestor of the specifically affected v4.5.1 release, satisfying the introduction side of the version boundary. No patched side exists because the same mechanism remains in v4.6.1 and current HEAD, so null fix SHAs are justified as unpatched rather than unknown. Finally, the verdict uses only the BIC commit object: it has human author/committer Aaron Turner and no AI/bot/co-author/generated trailer. The source header's attribution to an earlier independent student project explains provenance but is not a commit-object AI signal. Therefore the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched: no commit or release in the validated full history bounds attacker-controlled IPv4 ip_len by the pcap buffer's caplen before do_checksum_math_liveplay, so no fix_sha, direct_fix_sha, or patched version boundary exists to record. This is a remediation gap, not missing evidence for the NOT_AI attribution.
